column3: Close to the Hebrew; “your report” is rendered “your speech,” “I fear” “was afraid,” and “to have compassion” “mercy.”
Close to the Hebrew; the present “he comes” is rendered as past, “came.”
Close to the Hebrew; “two horns” is rendered “rays flashing.”
Close to the Hebrew; “plague (resheph)” is rendered “fever.”
Close to the Hebrew; the verb glossed “shook” is rendered “measured,” and “they have been shattered” “were scattered.”
Close to the Hebrew; “under trouble” is rendered “in affliction.”
NKJV renders the difficult “your bow is made bare; oaths [of] arrows, a word” as “Your bow was made quite ready; Oaths were sworn over Your arrows”; the meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “they writhe” is rendered “trembled,” and “a downpour” “The overflowing.”
NKJV renders “for the salvation of your anointed” as “For salvation with Your Anointed,” capitalized, and “the chief” as “the head.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the head of his warriors” is rendered “The head of his villages”; the meaning of the word is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “you trod on the sea” is rendered “You walked through the sea.”

NKJV renders “my belly” as “my body,” and “that I must wait quietly for the day of trouble to come up on the people who attack us” as “That I might rest in the day of trouble. When he comes up to the people, He will invade them with his troops.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Yahweh the Lord” is rendered “The LORD God,” “like the does” “like deer’s feet,” and “my high places” “my high hills.”
